title: Priority Hedging & Deterministic Tool Replay - PRD (draft)
content:
Overview:
This document proposes a combined server-side priority hedging mechanism and a deterministic tool-replay contract for the Hosted API. Goal is to reduce tail latency impact from slow tool integrations and unreliable downstream services while preserving deterministic replayability for debugging, audits, and consistent client-side UX across retries or fallback model variants.

Problem statement:
- Customers building tool-driven agents experience nondeterministic behaviour when tool calls are retried or hedged: multiple in-flight calls, duplicated side-effects, and varying final outputs depending on timing.
- Tail latency from third-party tools (search, knowledge bases, SaaS APIs) inflates overall token latency and breaks latency SLOs.
- Developers need a predictable, debuggable contract for tool invocation that supports client-side replay and server-side hedging without producing duplicate external effects.

Design principles:
- Safety-first: hedging must avoid duplicate side-effects. Default behaviour should be safe-by-default (idempotency/side-effect guard rails).
- Predictability: the protocol must allow deterministic replay of a session given a recorded event stream plus a compact replay manifest.
- Low-friction SDK ergonomics: expose simple primitives that map to common patterns (sync tool, async observable tool, hedged tool).
- Incremental adoption: work with existing streaming frames; fall back to non-hedged behaviour if client/SDK doesn't opt-in.

User personas and pain points:
- ML engineers embedding tool orchestration into prompts: need consistent testable behaviour across runs and model variants.
- Backend integrators: want hedging to reduce tail latency but cannot accept duplicate side-effects from third-party systems.
- Mobile/web frontend engineers: need compact, deterministic session artifacts to resume UX after network flaps.

High-level solution
1) Priority hedging policy on the server: lightweight configurable rules that spawn backup requests to alternative tool providers or lower-cost model variants when a primary tool exceeds a hedging threshold. Hedging decisions are observable and recorded.
2) Deterministic tool-replay manifest: every invocation that can produce external effects is recorded to an append-only event stream containing a canonical request id (rid), idempotency token (if provided), intent-hash, tool contract, chosen provider, and chosen timing. A compact replay manifest (list of rids + provider decisions) can fully reconstruct the order and outcomes required to replay the session deterministically against mock or dry-run tool endpoints.
3) Safe hedging mode: for side-effectful tools, hedging is limited to speculative reads only; write operations require explicit opt-in and server-side guards (e.g., two-phase commit pattern or delegated write proxies).

API surface (draft):
- New top-level request fields: 
  - hedging: { mode: "opt-in" | "safe" | "off", policy: "latency" | "cost" | "redundancy", thresholds: { p95_ms } } (SDKs will expose ergonomic overloads instead of raw objects)
  - replay_token: opaque string used to anchor deterministic replay manifests
  - tool_idempotency_hint: string optional to help server detect duplicate intent
- Streaming frame additions: 
  - FRAME_TOOL_INVOCATION_START: { rid, tool_name, provider_candidates, intent_hash }
  - FRAME_TOOL_INVOCATION_DECISION: { rid, chosen_provider, timestamp, hedged:boolean }
  - FRAME_TOOL_RESULT: { rid, status: ok|fail|timeout|fallback, body_ref }
  - FRAME_REPLAY_MANIFEST: emitted at end-of-session when requested: { replay_token, rids: [..], decisions: [...] }

Deterministic replay semantics:
- The server must ensure that for a given replay_token + event stream, the decision ordering and provider choices are deterministic.
- For hedged reads (e.g., search), the server will select the earliest successful response and record which candidate won. Replaying against mocked providers that return the recorded winner response will reproduce the session.
- For side-effectful tools, the manifest records whether a write was executed, which provider accepted it, and a canonical result id; the SDK will expose a dry-run mode where side-effects are not actually executed but the manifest can still be generated for validation.

SDK ergonomics (hosted-api SDKs - JS/Python):
- Provide high-level helpers: hedgedToolCall(toolSpec, {mode, fallbackProviders, timeout}) that returns a streaming iterator or promise depending on call type.
- Default hedgedToolCall is safe: if the toolSpec declares "idempotent":false, SDK will require explicit allowSideEffects:true to enable hedging-writes.
- Standardized callback for replay manifests: onReplayManifest(manifest) -> developer can persist manifest alongside application logs.
- Easy toggles for dev/prod: SDK flag RW_HEDGING=on|off|safe to let teams test locally without hedging.

Backpressure & priority handling:
- Introduce priority hints at the request and per-tool-call level (high|normal|background). Server batching will maintain weighted fairness; hedging thresholds are priority-aware (higher priority => lower hedging threshold).
- For mobile clients, SDK will use a low-bandwidth hedging policy that prefers local cache/mocks as secondary candidates rather than network-heavy hedges.

Observability and telemetry:
- Emit per-rid telemetry: start_ts, chosen_provider, hedged(bool), upstream_latency_ms, result_status.
- Console dashboard: new "Tool Reliability" panel showing hedged call rates, success-by-provider, and cost delta from hedging.
- Alerts: regression alert when hedged success rate drops below X% or hedging increases cost by Y% over baseline.

Safety & compliance notes:
- Side-effectful hedging disabled by default for enterprise customers without explicit agreement.
- Replay manifests contain provider identifiers and timestamps; for regulated customers we will support redaction and encryption-at-rest via existing KMS integrations.

Migration path and incremental rollout:
- Phase 1 (MVP): server-side hedging for read-only tool calls; streaming frame additions; SDK helpers in JS only; manual replay manifest request API.
- Phase 2: deterministic replay for side-effectful tools with dry-run and delegated write proxies; add Python SDK helpers; start console panels.
- Phase 3: automatic canary rollout: routers can apply hedging per-customer based on usage tiers; SLO-backed default policies for Dedicated customers.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How do we prove strong determinism when provider selection is time-dependent? (Answer: record winner + canonical timestamps; support mock-by-response-id.)
- Cost implications of hedging vs value of SLO improvements for customers — need benchmarking across common workloads.
- UX complexity: how to keep SDK API small while allowing advanced policy control?

Milestones & success metrics:
- M1 (6 weeks): prototyped hedging controller + streaming frames; internal dogfood with two product teams. Metric: 30% reduction in 99th latency for read-heavy toolchains in dogfood.
- M2 (12 weeks): public JS SDK release + replay manifest persistence primitive. Metric: 80% of test-suite replays are bit-identical when executed against mock provider responses.
- M3 (20 weeks): beta feature for safe hedged writes with delegated proxies for 3 enterprise customers. Metric: zero duplicated writes in production dogfood over a 30d window.

Appendix: example streaming trace (simplified)
- Client sends request with hedging:{mode:safe,policy:latency,p95_ms:300}
- FRAME_TOOL_INVOCATION_START {rid: r123, tool_name: kb_search, provider_candidates:[kb-v1, kb-v2], intent_hash: h9}
- kb-v1 timed out at 260ms; server hedges to kb-v2 at 300ms threshold
- FRAME_TOOL_INVOCATION_DECISION {rid:r123, chosen_provider: kb-v2, timestamp: 2024-11-12T15:21:30Z, hedged:true}
- FRAME_TOOL_RESULT {rid:r123, status:ok, body_ref: b55}
- At session end, FRAME_REPLAY_MANIFEST contains r123 -> kb-v2 mapping so replays will pick kb-v2 first.

Next steps:
- Engineering: spike on hedging controller + lightweight event store for rids (owner: Jonah Kim).
- SDK: prototype hedgedToolCall JS helper and replay manifest callback (owner: Marco Alvarez).
- Product: run two customer-facing playtests in controlled eval environments (owner: Aisha Patel).

Notes to reviewers:
- Please focus review on determinism guarantees and the safety model for side-effects.
- If your team maintains a tool provider integration (search, embeddings-store, CRM connectors), ping the owners so we can collect provider failure characteristics for realistic benchmarks.
